title: Space-bounded timed conditional composition
statement: Let $D$, $M_1$, and $M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet; let $p$ be a predicate on Boolean words, let $f_1,f_2$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, let $T_0,T_1,T_2$ map natural numbers to natural numbers, and let $s_D,s_1,s_2$ map natural numbers to natural numbers. Suppose $D$ computes $[p(x)]$ in time $T_0(|x|)$, $M_i$ computes $f_i(x)$ in time $T_i(|x|)$ for $i=1,2$, and for every Boolean word $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the space used by each machine $D,M_1,M_2$ by time $t$ is at most $s_D(|x|),s_1(|x|),s_2(|x|)$, respectively. Then there are a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $M$ computes the function equal to $f_1(x)$ when $p(x)$ is true and $f_2(x)$ otherwise in time $c\bigl(T_0(|x|)+\max(T_1(|x|),T_2(|x|))+1\bigr)$, and for every $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$ its space use by time $t$ is at most $s_D(|x|)+\max(s_1(|x|),s_2(|x|))+c$.

$f_1,f_2$ map Boolean words to Boolean words

For every $x,t$, the space used by $M_1$ by time $t$ is at most $s_1(|x|)$
For every $x,t$, the space used by $M_2$ by time $t$ is at most $s_2(|x|)$
